Under your rules, 7 of the 10 expected species were called present and 1 called species is not on the list.

I computed this directly from the report rather than using `mockcheck`, so the result follows your stated rules exactly. The report has 20 species-level rows totalling 237,500 clade reads. After renormalising to 100%, 8 species are at or above 0.1%. Nothing else is close to the cutoff: every remaining species is below 0.05%.

| Species (as reported) | % of species reads | Status |
|---|---|---|
| limosilactobacillus fermentum (counted as lactobacillus fermentum) | 61.52 | expected |
| bacillus spizizenii | 15.95 | **not expected** |
| enterococcus faecalis | 14.62 | expected |
| pseudomonas aeruginosa | 3.80 | expected |
| staphylococcus aureus | 1.51 | expected |
| salmonella enterica | 1.29 | expected |
| escherichia coli | 0.92 | expected |
| listeria monocytogenes | 0.34 | expected |

- **Not called:** bacillus subtilis, saccharomyces cerevisiae and cryptococcus neoformans. None of them reach 0.1%.
- **Possible naming issue:** bacillus spizizenii is closely related to B. subtilis and was formerly a subspecies of it. The 15.95% here may really be the expected B. subtilis reads under a different name. Your rules allow only the fermentum rename, so I counted it as a false call. If you merged it, the result would be 8 found and 0 false.
- **The abundances are far from the expected profile.** The truth file expects 12% for each bacterium, but L. fermentum takes about 62
